title: Valid Palindrome
keyIdea: Compare from both ends inward. left and right each skip anything that isn't a letter or digit, then the two characters must match ignoring case. Meet in the middle with no mismatch → palindrome. No cleaned copy needed.

approaches.name: Clean, then compare with reverse
approaches.idea: Build a new string with only the letters and digits, lower-cased. It's a palindrome if it equals its own reverse.
approaches.why: One pass to build the cleaned string, one to reverse it, one to compare. Two extra strings of up to n characters.

approaches.name: Two pointers, skip in place
approaches.idea: left from the start, right from the end. Each skips non-alphanumerics, then compare tolower(s[left]) and tolower(s[right]). Mismatch → false. Match → both move inward.
approaches.why: left only moves right and right only moves left, so together they touch each character at most once. Only two int variables.

quiz.q: Why do the inner skip loops also check left < right?
options: So a string of only punctuation can't push left past the end, and the pointers don't cross while skipping
true: after skipping there's nothing left, and empty counts as a palindrome

quiz.q: Why is the two-pointer version O(n) even with loops inside a loop?
options: left and right only ever move inward, so each character is visited at most once in total
The inner loops run at most once

steps: Which characters count? Is 'A' the same as 'a'? Do digits count? What about an empty or all-space string?
Do "race a car" and "0P" by hand. Why is " " true?
Clean the string and compare with its reverse: time and space?
Compare the two ends and move inward: which pattern? What lets you avoid the cleaned copy?
What does each pointer skip, and what stops the skip loops running past each other?
Code it, saying tolower and "letter or digit" out loud.
Dry-run "race a car": which pair fails first?
Time and space? How would LC 680 (allowed to delete one character) change it?
